grh_64abaad9bdb793820819.title: The Ouija Spells Murder
paragraphs: Ellie and her friends casually experiment with a Ouija board while their city is terrorized by a serial killer known as the sidewalk slasher. The board produces messages telling them to find the killer, go to Clover Heights and contact the police. Following the clues leads them to a house already connected with a legitimate suspect and to the alley where the latest victim was found. Police Lieutenant Connors appears to take their strange story seriously and escorts the women through the investigation, but later reveals himself as the murderer when he hides in their car and threatens them with a knife. Their friend Bill arrives in a cab at the crucial moment, and the driver tackles Connors before he can escape. Safely home, the group is amazed that the Ouija board led them first to the crime scene and then to the actual killer, but their promise to stop using it lasts only until another ominous message begins to spell itself out.

This [[show|sears-radio-theater|Sears Radio Theater]] broadcast aired on February 21, 1979. It is listed as episode 13 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Louise Heath, Joan McCall, Sam Edwards, Howard Culver, and Shepard Menken. Other credited names include Elliott Lewis as director, Elliott Lewis as producer, Shirley Gordon as writer, and [[person|vincent-price|Vincent Price]] as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_6422caba8c5ab4cef191.title: The Pirate of New Orleans
paragraphs: Pirate Jean Lafitte slips into New Orleans in disguise, where he meets Suzanne and begins to imagine what it would mean to belong to the city rather than merely raid its waters. When the British offer him gold to guide their fleet, Lafitte instead offers his men and knowledge to the Americans for the defense of New Orleans. The governor refuses to bargain with a pirate, but General Jackson accepts the help, and after the battle Lafitte and his men receive a full pardon and citizenship. Even with Suzanne asking him to stay, Lafitte decides that respectable life is not his and returns to the sea, still listening for the city he helped save.
